chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Leon Rene and When the Swallows Came Back to Capistrano
summary: Joe recalls working with Leon Rene, the songwriter, and tells of a late recording of Mister Satchmo before Rene died.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Darensbourg - 144

Yes. But I had came here in '26. But I didn't go to work with Mutt then. Because we had played around here... We had a fairly big band. Then I worked sometimes with... before I went with Mutt (it wasn't a steady job, though), Leon René, that wrote "When The Swallows Came Back To Capistrano" and...
Did he write that?
Yes, and "Sleepy Time Down South."
I knew he wrote "Sleepy Time Down South."
Yeah, him and Clarence Muse. Leon and his brother...
Otis?
...Otis and Clarence Muse wrote... I think Clarence Muse was the co-writer on "When The Swallows Come Back To Capistrano."
I didn't know that. I know the piece; I recorded that thing myself.

Oh, yeah. That is still a big number. For instance, just as a little sidelight, every time it comes around from "When The Swallows Came Back To Capistrano." Leon would usually go to Capistrano, and they'd usually have to move the TV cameras and everything, and he would sing it.
I'll be darned.
Darensbourg - 145
Just a matter for ceremonies.
Capistrano is down the beach somewhere, isn't it.
That's right. Not far from there. Maybe... It's got to be 60 or 70 miles.
Let me get this straight. It has nothing to do with Jazz, but it just clarifies this. The swallows migrate from this place, and then later (?) they come back.
That's right, they leave, and they come back practically the same day -- every year.
Still? Now?

Oh, yes. And this year I think was the first or second year... Because Leon just died. And when he died, he was in the process of writing... Motown Records was going to produce a film on Louis, and Leon wrote a tune called "Mister Satchmo," a pretty thing, nice words and everything. And he wanted a record of it to submit to Motown, so we made it, not long before he died.
Just this last year or two.

Off of that, he was going to make an album -- because we had talked about it. In fact, he's got a son that's living, who is still talking about it. However, like I said, naturally we didn't get to make the album. And I think this is the first year he missed it. Well, he died.
Darensbourg - 146
That will make you miss it.
I think so! But Leon had a band, a big band. Leon never was a good player, really. But he was a good writer; he wrote a lot of good songs.
